lesson: A downstream counterfactual margin is not interpretable unless the supposedly decisive source representation itself discriminates the target from the matched foil. Validate source-level separability before attributing a small downstream margin drop to model ignorance or insufficient capacity.
action: insert a source-separability gate before downstream causal attribution; if source pooling is non-discriminative, diagnose upstream representation geometry rather than repairing or scaling downstream modules

lesson: Full-sentence cosine can be a poor probe for value identity when target and foil share subject, attribute, syntax, and nearly all tokens. A probe may report high semantic similarity while failing to preserve the small but decision-critical value distinction.
action: separate raw token/span value information from pooled sentence geometry and use query-conditioned/value-aware probes when the decision hinges on a small lexical/value change

lesson: Do not scale a downstream module to satisfy a validator whose upstream source representation is itself non-discriminative. Scaling decisions require a valid measurement chain that isolates a real capacity bottleneck.
action: keep scale uncapped but defer capacity changes until upstream discrimination is validated and a downstream failure persists on independent untouched data
